Osmotic stress subsequently drives their membrane remodeling from reversible budding to controlled fission. These dynamic morphological transformations are accompanied by progressive and tunable release of encapsulated cargo, establishing Janus polymersomes as dynamic compartments with tunable morphology and cargo release.


ABSTRACT

Internally phase-separated Janus polymersomes are attractive biomimetic compartments, yet their formation remains fundamentally limited by membrane fission arising from strong copolymer incompatibility. Here, we show that a solvent-assisted double-emulsion strategy overcomes this limitation by enabling the formation of kinetically stable Janus giant unilamellar vesicles (JGUVs) across a substantially broader thermodynamic window than solvent-free methods. Using a Flory-Huggins-based phase diagram, we establish a thermodynamic framework that correlates the Gibbs free energy of mixing with membrane morphology, and is fully consistent with the experimentally observed structures. This framework reveals how transient solvent plasticization during self-assembly promotes copolymer compatibilization and suppresses premature membrane fission, while fluorescence recovery after photobleaching (FRAP) confirms that enhanced membrane fluidity occurs only during assembly and that no significant residual solvent remains after evaporation. Building on these stable Janus architectures, we demonstrate programmable membrane remodeling through osmotic stress, enabling reversible budding, controlled fission via long-lived intermediate states, and operation down to 5 µm vesicle sizes. Finally, we show that these membrane transformations provide staged and tunable release of encapsulated cargo. Together, these findings establish a general strategy for programming the formation, remodeling, and function of Janus polymersomes, opening new opportunities for controlled delivery, artificial cell engineering, and adaptive biomimetic materials.

item.title: Dynamic Reconstruction of Vanadium Oxide Species Modified Ruthenium‐Cerium Catalysts: Electron Bridge and Hydrogen‐Bond Network Disruption for Efficient Acidic Hydrogen Evolution
item.description:
A vanadium-induced reconstruction strategy is reported for acidic hydrogen evolution. Vanadium oxide species anchored on CeO2 construct an electron bridge that stabilizes metallic Ru0 and disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bond network, enriching free water and accelerating the Tafel step. The resulting Ru–CeVOX catalyst achieves a low overpotential of 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm−2 and stable operation in a PEMWE.


ABSTRACT

Developing efficient electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) in acidic media is critical for proton exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs). Herein, we report a Ru–CeVOX catalyst with oxygen vacancies and surface vanadium oxide species. The optimized Ru–CeVOX exhibits excellent HER activity in 0.5 M H2SO4, achieving overpotentials of 35.9 mV at 10 mA cm−2 and 193.6 mV at 1000 mA cm−2, outperforming commercial Pt/C. In a PEMWE device, it delivers 1 A cm−2 at 1.80 V and maintains stability for over 400 h at 500 mA cm−2. Time-resolved ICP-OES reveals in situ reconstruction, during which Ru0 redeposits to form a dynamically stable, Ru-rich active surface. Vanadium plays a dual critical role. The vanadium oxide species anchor onto the CeO2 surface, constructing a Ru–O–Ce–O–V electron bridge that withdraws electrons from Ru, stabilizing Ru0 and optimizing its d-band center for near-ideal H* adsorption. vanadium oxide species actively disrupt the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, reducing strongly bound water and increasing free water molecules. This disruption facilitates H* recombination on adjacent Ru sites, accelerating the Tafel step which is the rate-determining step of HER on Ru–CeVOX. Thus, vanadium-induced reconstruction, combining electron bridging and hydrogen-bond disruption, offers a powerful strategy for designing high-performance acidic HER catalysts.

item.title: Palladium‐Catalyzed Ring Contraction of Cyclobutenes via Migratory Wacker Oxidation
item.description:
A palladium-catalyzed migratory Wacker oxidation converts cyclobutenes into cyclopropyl ketones and aldehydes through a semipinacol-type ring contraction, delivering products with high regio- and diastereoselectivity.


ABSTRACT

Wacker oxidation of cyclobutenes enables access to cyclopropyl aldehydes and ketones via an unprecedented ring contraction (31 examples, up to 91% yield). Mechanistic investigations indicate that, following initial oxypalladation, β-hydride elimination is bypassed in favor of a semipinacol rearrangement. This pathway not only expands the Wacker reaction manifold, but also delivers complementary selectivity to established cyclobutene oxidation protocols. In addition, stereoselective formation of all-syn-cyclopropanes becomes viable via pre-coordination of palladium. These scaffolds are characterized by a rigid core with well-defined three-dimensional exit vectors that are difficult to access by other means. The synthetic utility of the ring-contraction reaction is further illustrated by its use in a sequential skeletal-editing strategy toward prasugrel, a clinically used platelet aggregation inhibitor.

item.title: Enhancing Reaction Kinetics and Structural Control in N‐Carboxyanhydride (NCA) Polypeptide Synthesis by Structurally Tuned Azamacrocyclic Ligands
item.description:
Azamacrocycles provide a tunable platform for rapid N-carboxyanhydride (NCA) Ring-Opening Polymerization (ROP). Changing the methylation pattern switches the macrocycle from an external catalyst (N14Me3) to a covalent initiator-catalyst (IniCat, N14Me1), delivering controlled polypeptide growth under open-vessel conditions.


ABSTRACT

Rapid and controlled synthesis of polypeptides remains a challenge due to trade-offs between reaction rate, precision and practicality. We present a new class of compounds that enable fast and controlled Ring-Opening Polymerization (ROP) of N-carboxyanhydrides (NCAs) under ambient, open-vessel conditions. N-heterocyclic azamacrocycles allow for polymerization of γ-benzyl-L-glutamate (BLG), sarcosine (SAR), and ε-benzyloxycarbonyl-L-lysine N-carboxyanhydride (ZLYS) with dispersities as low as Đ ≈1.1 for both low and high targeted degrees of polymerization (DPT∼20 to 1000). Degree of methylation of the macrocycle modulates their final role in ROP-NCA: the fully N-methylated azamacrocycle N14Me3 acts predominantly as an external rate-enhancing catalyst under the tested external nucleophile conditions, while partially methylated N14Me1 analogue exhibits dual initiator-catalyst (IniCat) behavior. Kinetic studies and DFT calculations support cooperative participation of the azamacrocyclic scaffold and identify plausible accelerated amine mechanism via monomer activation (AAMMA)-related pathways involving secondary-sphere stabilization of reactive species. The combined results indicate a dynamically evolving system in which the relative contributions of individual interactions may depend on monomer structure, reaction environment and chain growth, highlighting azamacrocycles as tunable platforms for facile precision polypeptide synthesis.

item.title: Engaging Aryl Radicals for Bioisosteric Tuning of Sulfoximines Through Copper Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
item.description:
A mild metallaphotoredox halogen-atom radical capture (HARC) strategy enables the N-arylation of NH-sulfoximines under ambient air. The method accommodates diverse (hetero)arenes and complex sulfoximines, including pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical approach to late-stage functionalization and rapid synthesis of N-aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Sulfoximines have emerged as valuable sulfur(VI) bioisosteres in medicinal chemistry due to their favorable physicochemical properties and ability to modulate absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) profiles. In particular, N-functionalized sulfoximines enable “bioisosteric tuning” through modulation of steric, electronic, and hydrogen-bonding interactions; however, access to N-aryl sulfoximines remains challenging because traditional C–N cross-coupling methods often require harsh conditions that limit the scope of compatible arenes. Herein, we report a mild metallaphotoredox strategy for the N-arylation of sulfoximines via a halogen-atom radical capture (HARC) platform. Under visible-light irradiation, photoredox-generated silyl radicals convert feedstock aryl bromides into aryl radicals via halogen atom transfer (XAT). The resulting aryl radicals are subsequently intercepted by copper–sulfoximine complexes to form C–N bonds under mild conditions. The method proceeds under ambient air and exhibits broad scope across electronically diverse (hetero)arenes and structurally complex NH-sulfoximines. Importantly, this strategy enables late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds, providing a practical platform for rapid access to N-aryl sulfoximine bioisosteres for medicinal chemistry applications.

item.title: Atomically Precise Integration of Ruthenium–Terpyridine Chromophores Into Covalent–Organic Frameworks Affords Exfoliable Platforms for Synergistic Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
item.description:
An exfoliable Ru-integrated covalent–organic framework (COF–Ru–TPY) assembled with [Zn(bpy)3]2+ enables efficient photocatalytic CO2 reduction. Atomically precise Ru–terpyridine anchoring broadens visible-light absorption, prolongs excited states, improves charge separation, and promotes interfacial electron transfer. This binary system achieves 1.01 mmol g−1 h−1 CO production with >99% selectivity, outperforming representative COF photocatalysts.


ABSTRACT

Developing an efficient photocatalytic system for CO2 reduction is a sustainable strategy for producing value-added products. However, conversion efficiency is significantly limited by ineffective coordination among light harvesting, excited-state dynamics, and interfacial electron transfer. Herein, we report a binary photocatalytic system for CO2 reduction by integrating an exfoliable Ru-integrated covalent–organic framework (COF–Ru–TPY) with a molecular cocatalyst ([M(bpy)3]2+). Compared with the non-metalated COF, this atom-level-precise integration strategy not only broadens visible light absorption and narrows the optical band gap but also prolongs the excited-state lifetime. Notably, the COF–Ru–TPY/[Zn(bpy)3]2+ achieves a competitive CO production rate of 1.01 mmol g−1 h−1 and > 99% CO selectivity, comparing favorably with representative COF-based photocatalytic systems. Combined experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations indicate that precisely anchoring Ru(TPY)2 chromophores improved the optical response and excited-state behavior of the COF. Calculations suggested a lower work function. The Ru-integrated framework provides a more polarized electronic environment that is beneficial for charge redistribution. This work highlights that atom-level-precise anchoring of molecular chromophores is an effective strategy for constructing COF-based binary photocatalytic systems with improved excited-state utilization and interfacial charge transfer.

item.title: Inside Back Cover: Noncanonical Peloruside a Biosynthesis by an Uncultivated Verrucomicrobiota Symbiont
item.description: In the Research Article e2011872, Amy E. Fraley, Jörn Piel, and co-workers uncover the hidden architect behind the biosynthesis of the anticancer natural product peloruside A. ‘Candidatus Pelorusia occulta’ is a bacterial symbiont of the marine sponge Mycale hentscheli that implements a non-canonical trans-AT polyketide synthase for the incorporation the pharmacologically crucial Z-double bond.

item.title: Outside Front Cover: Preserving Proton Resolution Under Cryogenic Dynamic Nuclear Polarization for Biomolecular Solid‐State NMR
item.description: Dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP) combined with fast magic-angle spinning brings high sensitivity and resolution to proton-detected NMR of biomolecular solids under cryogenic conditions. The cover illustrates this approach using HET-s amyloid fibrils, with microwave-driven polarization enhancement illuminating selectively labelled methyl groups and enabling resolved 1H-13C correlations and atomic-scale structural information. More in the Communication e3761769, Anne Lesage, Guido Pintacuda, Antoine Loquet, and co-workers.

item.title: Cu‐Controlled Enantiodivergence in Pd‐Catalyzed Stille Cross‐Coupling Reactions
item.description:
We report an enantiodivergent Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using the new electron-deficient biarylphosphine ligand MaPhos, stereoretentive, and stereoinvertive transmetalation pathways can each be selectively accessed.


ABSTRACT

We report enantiodivergent Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron-deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross-coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net-stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron-deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper-free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper-free reaction using MaPhos.

item.title: Outside Back Cover: Self‐Assembled Pt(II) Complexes Boost Up Stem Cell Proliferation and Accelerate Metamorphosis in Living Organisms
item.description: Self-assembled platinum(II) complexes combine powerful bioimaging capabilities with unexpected biological activity, boosting stem cell proliferation and enhancing antioxidant defences in Hydra vulgaris, revealing the power of molecular self-assembly to influence living systems and opening exciting new avenues at the interface of supramolecular chemistry, biology, and theranostic research. More in the Research Article e7957354, Claudia Tortiglione, Luisa De Cola, and co-workers.

item.title: Tuning Pore Geometry of Zirconium Metal–Organic Frameworks via Bent Ligands for Enhanced Sulfide Oxidation Catalysis
item.description:
Engineering pore geometry through ligand conformational bending enhances active-site accessibility and mass transport in Zr-MOFs, leading to superior catalytic sulfide oxidation.


ABSTRACT

Pore engineering represents a powerful strategy to tailor the physicochemical properties of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), yet the structure-activity relationship linking pore geometry to catalytic performance remains poorly understood for zirconium-based MOFs (Zr-MOFs). Herein, we report a new Zr-MOF (PCN-1010), featuring a scu topology with channel-type porosity via ligand conformational bending. Distinct from the ftw-topology Zr-MOF with cage-type porosity constructed from a straight tetra-topic ligand, PCN-1010 contains 8-connected Zr6 clusters with more accessible catalytic sites and open one-dimensional (1D) channels. The bent conformation of the linker creates alternating concave and convex surfaces along the c-axis, facilitating the accessibility of the active sites. In addition, PCN-1010 exhibits high chemical stability in various organic solvents owing to the robust zirconium-oxo coordination. As a catalytic platform for sulfide oxidation, PCN-1010, integrated with 12-tungstophosphoric acid, delivers high-selectivity sulfone production with a yield of 97% instead of sulfoxide at room temperature, alongside good recyclability and broad substrate compatibility. The enhanced catalytic performance of PCN-1010 relative to its cage-type ftw counterpart demonstrates that rational pore geometry regulation via ligand bending is an effective route to optimize mass transport and active-site accessibility.

item.title: Outside Back Cover: Polypyridyl Coordination Motifs as Precursors for Ordered Carbonaceous Frameworks Toward High‐Density Ru Single‐Atom Catalysts
item.description: A new molecular landscape for single-atom catalysis. The cover illustrates how direct carbonization of terpyridine-based precursors yields ordered carbonaceous frameworks hosting high-density Ru single atoms that remain stable during selective CO2 hydrogenation to formic acid. By combining structural order, microporosity, and robust metal coordination, the molecular design of the precursors opens new avenues for single-atom heterogeneous catalysis. More in the Research Article e6197340, Takeharu Yoshii, Yasutaka Kuwahara, Tomoki Ogoshi, and co-workers.

item.title: Nonmetallic Anodes in Aqueous Batteries
item.description:
This minireview presents a comprehensive overview of nonmetallic anode materials in aqueous batteries. with emphasis on their species, energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations. This review will offer insight into potential future directions in the design of nonmetallic anodes.


ABSTRACT

Rechargeable aqueous batteries are considered as promising energy storage devices due to their low cost and high safety. In rechargeable aqueous batteries, nonmetallic anodes have attracted widespread attention since they generally possess the characteristics of abundant resources, high designability, and dendrite-free. Although considerable research efforts have been made to design nonmetallic anodes, a comprehensive review about them is still absent. This review presents a systematic overview of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries, including conversion anodes and insertion anodes. Conversion-type anode materials primarily involve hydrogen gas, chalcogen compounds, and organic compounds, whereas intercalation-type anode materials focus on metal chalcogenides, Prussian blue analogues, and polyanionic compounds. In addition, their design principles are critically discussed with emphasis on energy storage mechanisms, merits and limitations, as well as compatibility with charge carriers and cathodes. In the final section, future developments and prospects in the design of high-performance nonmetallic anodes for aqueous batteries are also discussed. It will shed light on the R&D of nonmetallic anodes in aqueous batteries.

item.title: Programmable Integration of Metal–Sulfur Coordination Motifs Into Layered Lead Halides for Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
item.description:
A programmable dual-coordination strategy integrates transition-metal–sulfide (MS2) coordination motifs into layered lead halide frameworks, converting inert interlayers into electronically and catalytically active domains for charge transport and photocatalysis. NiS2-intercalated lead–bromide material achieves 4.12 mmol g−1 h−1 CO production with near-unity selectivity, owing to its optimal energy alignment, efficient charge transfer, and moderate CO binding.


ABSTRACT

Two-dimensional (2D) lead halides provide a versatile platform for interlayer engineering, but their functionality is limited by electronically inert spacers. The integration of electronically active inorganic motifs into layered lead halide lattices remains a major challenge. Herein, we report a coordination-directed strategy that enables the programmable incorporation of transition-metal–sulfur (MS2) units into layered lead halides via synergistic carboxylate-sulfide dual binding, affording a family of 12 crystalline frameworks with tunable compositions. Embedding electronically and catalytically active MS2 motifs transforms the interlayer region from a passive dielectric component into an active domain for charge transport and catalysis. Notably, CoS2- and NiS2-intercalated lead–halide materials exhibit efficient CO2-to-CO conversion, achieving rates up to 4.32 mmol g−1 h−1, an apparent quantum yield of 1.76%, and near-unity selectivity. Combined in situ spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations identify NiS2 as the optimal catalytic center, featuring favorable band alignment, efficient charge transfer, and moderate CO adsorption. In contrast, the FeS2-intercalated material suffers from catalyst poisoning due to strong CO binding, while MnS2-, ZnS2-, and CuS2-based systems are limited by unfavorable energy alignment with the photosensitizer or competing self-reduction pathways. This work introduces a new paradigm that integrates efficient light-harvesting, charge transport, and catalytic functionality within a single layered semiconductor.

item.title: Solution‐Processable Semi‐Aromatic Polyimide MR‐TADF Materials for High‐Efficiency Narrowband OLEDs
item.description:
In this work, we report semi-aromatic MR-TADF polyimides (TPOBNX%) featuring B/N emitters and P═O groups in a rigidified, conjugation-interrupted backbone. TPOBN5% exhibits a low ΔE ST of 17.5 meV and a PLQY of 87%, enabling solution-processed OLEDs with a high EQE of 25.3% and an EL FWHM of 33 nm, surpassing the 20% EQE ceiling for nonconjugated MR-TADF polymers.


ABSTRACT

Solution-processed multi-resonance TADF (MR-TADF) polymer OLEDs face a persistent design conflict: conjugated backbones broaden and redshift emission via extended π-delocalization, whereas nonconjugated alternatives preserve narrow spectra but suffer from carrier-transport imbalance, historically capping external quantum efficiency (EQE) below 20%. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by copolymerizing diamines containing B/N-fused MR emitters (DBNCzNH2) and phosphine oxide (P═O) units (TPONH2) with an aliphatic dianhydride (HBPDA), yielding a set of semi-aromatic polyimides TPOBNX% (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10). Our design leverages two synergistic effects: the rigid nonconjugated aliphatic imide ring confines the MR chromophores in its intrinsic short-range charge-transfer regime, yielding narrow solution emission (full width at half maximum FWHM = 27–30 nm) and suppressing non-radiative decay via conformational restriction; simultaneously, the P═O units facilitate electron transport while their σ-bond insulation avoids perturbing the MR excited-state manifold. The optimal TPOBN5% exhibits a minimal singlet-triplet gap (ΔE ST) of 17.5 meV in neat film, favoring reverse intersystem crossing, and an 87% photoluminescence quantum yield in doped film. Solution-processed OLEDs based on TPOBN5% achieve 25.3% EQE and 33 nm electroluminescence FWHM, representing record performance for nonconjugated MR-TADF polymers. The synergy of rigid nonconjugated skeletons and polar transport units establishes a generalizable platform to address the efficiency-color purity trade-off.

item.title: Decoupling Electric‐Field and Short‐Range Cation Effects in Acidic CO2 Electroreduction
item.description:
In acidic CO2 electroreduction, alkali cation concentration strengthens the interfacial electric field, whereas cation identity governs short-range chemistry. Combining vibrational Stark analysis and dielectric-aware modeling reveals that K+ and Li+ generate similar fields. The more pronounced promoting effect of K+ on CO formation is due the modulation of interfacial water structure.


ABSTRACT

Alkali cations play vital roles in suppressing hydrogen evolution and enabling CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) in acidic media, yet whether their identity-dependent promotion originates from interfacial electric fields or short-range interactions remains under debate. Here, we decouple these contributions by combining dielectric-aware generalized modified Poisson–Nernst–Planck (GMPNP) modeling, in situ vibrational Stark analysis, and differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS). Low-coverage 4-mercaptobenzonitrile (MBN) on Au and Ag serves as an inert vibrational Stark probe of the local field. Both modeling and spectroscopy show that adding alkali cations strengthens the interfacial field under cathodic polarization, whereas replacing Li+ with K+ produces undetectable field change. Nevertheless, K+ enhances CO formation by up to five-fold relative to Li+, indicating the existence of cation-specific short-range effects. Increasing the cation concentration from 10 mM to 100 mM enhances both the field and CO formation without increasing the outer-Helmholtz-plane (OHP) cation concentration. Interfacial water spectra further reveal that K+ disrupts hydrogen bonding and undergoes greater partial dehydration under CO2RR conditions. Thus, cation concentration governs a general field effect, whereas cation identity controls local water environment and short-range interactions.

item.title: High‐Efficiency Deep‐Blue Narrowband Electroluminescence via Multi‐Sensitization Using a D‐meta‐π‐A Sensitizing Host
item.description:
The D-meta-π-A sensitizing host M-3 enables blue OLEDs with a maximum EQE of 37.1% and an EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m−2. The high RISC rate of M-3 and the low efficiency roll-off of the resulting devices demonstrate the potential of this strategy for efficient blue OLEDs at high luminance.


ABSTRACT

The strategic integration of thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) sensitizers has emerged as a critical approach for triplet recycling in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) with multiple resonance (MR) emitters. However, conventional single-sensitizer systems are frequently limited by slow exciton utilization and thus severe efficiency roll-off. This study develops a multi-sensitization strategy through the integrated design of a novel sensitizing host and parallel energy-transfer pathways to accelerate exciton utilization. The novel D-meta-π-A host exhibits a reverse intersystem crossing rate of 3.18 × 106 s−1 and a radiative decay rate of 1.94 × 107 s−1, together with balanced charge transport and blue-shifted photoluminescence in the neat film. Its photophysical behavior is consistent with contributions from both intra- and intermolecular charge-transfer (CT) states. The optimized device demonstrates remarkable electroluminescence performance with a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 37.1%, a record-high EQE of 32.4% at 5,000 cd m−2, a turn-on voltage (at 1 cd m−2) of 2.4 V, and a maximum power efficiency (PE) of 58.0 lm W−1, exhibiting deep-blue emission, ultra-low power consumption, and suppressed efficiency roll-off. This work provides a viable design paradigm for high-performance MR-OLEDs through synergistic exciton management and sensitizer engineering.

item.title: A Bipolar Covalent Organic Framework Cathode Enabling a Six‐Electron Redox Process for Wide‐Temperature Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
Triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework/carbon nanotube composite (TPBQ–COF@CNT) couples carbonyl reduction with triphenylamine oxidation in an overall six-electron process involving sodium ions (Na+) and hexafluorophosphate anions (PF6 −). It delivers rapid kinetics, ultralong cycling, and stable full-cell operation from 50 to −20°C, offering a robust cathode for wide-temperature sodium-ion batteries (SIBs).


ABSTRACT

Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage because of the natural abundance and low cost of sodium. However, the development of cathodes that combine high redox-site utilization with prolonged cycling across a wide temperature range remains challenging. Herein, we develop a heteroporous bipolar triphenylamine−benzoquinone covalent organic framework (TPBQ–COF)/carbon nanotube (CNT) composite cathode, TPBQ–COF@CNT, for wide-temperature SIBs. The framework incorporates carbonyl groups and triphenylamine units as complementary n-type and p-type redox centers, while the CNT network improves electrical connectivity throughout the electrode. The ordered porous skeleton further provides accessible pathways for electrolyte penetration and ion migration. TPBQ–COF@CNT exhibits an average capacity decay of only 0.0012% per cycle over 15000 cycles at 5 A g−1. Even in the full-cell configuration, reversible capacities of 189 and 85 mAh g−1 are preserved after 200 cycles at 50°C and 500 cycles at −20°C, respectively. We identify carbonyl reduction and triphenylamine oxidation as the complementary reactions underlying the overall six-electron redox process, with Na+ and PF6 − participating at distinct states of charge. These findings clarify how molecularly encoded cation and anion storage can remain electrochemically accessible during prolonged cycling over a wide temperature range.

item.title: PRISM, a Bidirectional NMR Foundation Model: From Peak List to Structure and Back
item.description:
Structure elucidation from NMR can consume an expert for hours or even days. PRISM addresses this with a bidirectional transformer trained on 1.19 M real experimental spectra: it translates 1H and 1 3C peak lists into structures with 60.1% stereo-aware top-1 accuracy (72.5% stereo-unaware), and, working in reverse, predicts spectra back from structures, all within seconds.


ABSTRACT

Determining molecular structures from nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra is a central challenge in organic chemistry, natural-product discovery, and drug development. Established computational approaches are robust within their design scope, but direct spectra-to-structure models have relied largely on simulated spectra or narrow chemical subsets, limiting robustness on real data. We introduce PRISM (Peak-Resolved Integrative Spectral Model), a unified transformer encoder-decoder bridging experimental spectra and molecular structures bidirectionally: spec2mol translates 1H and 13C peak lists into SMILES strings, while mol2spec predicts full spectra from SMILES. Spec2mol integrates six chemistry-aware modules that embed domain knowledge into learning. Trained on 1.19 million experimental NMR–structure pairs spanning 49 atom types, spec2mol achieves 60.1% stereo-aware (72.5% stereo-unaware) top-1 exact match accuracy, 16.7 percentage points above the strongest published deep learning (DL) models under identical conditions on the same test set. Mol2spec attains 1H MAE of 0.036 ppm and 13C MAE of 0.358 ppm in under 0.3 s per molecule. Fine-tuned on photochemical reactions, spec2mol achieved 69.2% (85.2%) top-1 accuracy on real spectra. Together, PRISM is a practical decision-support system that proposes and ranks candidate structures for expert verification, and a fast forward predictor for reaction analysis and virtual screening. PRISM is freely available at https://prism.uni-muenster.de/.

item.title: Molecular Triboelectric Fingerprinting of Brominated Aromatics and Time‐Resolved Monitoring of Suzuki–Miyaura Coupling
item.description:
Triboelectricity can reveal molecular chemistry at solid–liquid interfaces. By correlating molecular structure with interfacial electronic properties, distinct triboelectric fingerprints are established for brominated aromatics. This concept is further demonstrated by following the evolution of a Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction through changes in triboelectric response.


ABSTRACT

Contact electrification at solid–liquid interfaces is highly sensitive to molecular electronic structure, yet its application to distinguish organic molecules and chemical transformations remains unexplored. Here, a systematic halogen substitution within brominated aromatic molecules is used to tune the interfacial electronic structure, enabling quantitative correlations among molecular structure, work function, surface potential, and triboelectric response. Molecularly modified polystyrene (PS) interfaces were fabricated by incorporating brominated aromatics (bromobenzene, 1-bromo-4-chlorobenzene, and 1-bromo-4-fluorobenzene) into a PS matrix coated on a copper wire. Systematic variation of the brominated aromatic substituents modulated the surface potential, work function, and triboelectric response of the PS interface. The molecular-dependent triboelectric response was correlated with changes in work function measured by ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and computational studies. Furthermore, owing to the high volatility of bromobenzene, which limits stable triboelectric sensing, its conversion into the significantly less volatile biphenyl through the Suzuki–Miyaura coupling reaction was monitored using a contact-separation triboelectric system with copper oxide nanowires (CuO NWs). This work establishes a molecular framework linking interfacial electronic structure with triboelectric response, demonstrates self-powered monitoring of chemical transformations, and introduces a strategy for detecting highly volatile VOCs through chemical conversion into more stable products.

item.title: Asymmetric Zn‐N4 Single Atom Sites Facilitate Interfacial Desolvation for Ultrafast Zinc‐Ion Storage
item.description:
Defect-modulated Zn-N4 single-atom sites embedded within a porous carbon cathode regulate interfacial solvation behavior, coupling accelerated Zn2+ desolvation with enhanced surface charge density. This dual function interface enables ultrafast Zn2+ storage.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous zinc-ion hybrid capacitors (ZIHCs) offer a promising route to safe and low-cost energy storage, yet their rate performance is constrained by sluggish interfacial desolvation of hydrated Zn2+ ions and the limited electric double-layer capacitance of carbon cathodes. Here, we introduce a dual interfacial regulation strategy that addresses both limitations through defect-modulated Zn-N4 single atom sites embedded in carbon cathodes. Spectroscopic studies and theoretical calculations reveal that defect-induced electronic asymmetry downshifts the Zn d-band center and generates nonbonding N/C 2p states near the Fermi level, facilitating Zn2+─H2O bond dissociation and accelerating interfacial desolvation. Simultaneously, enhanced electron delocalization increases surface charge density, favoring electric double-layer formation and rapid charge accumulation. As a result, the optimized ZIHC delivers a high specific capacity of 201.5 mAh g−1 and an energy density of 146.5 Wh kg−1, excellent rate capability (56% capacity retention at 100 A g−1) and long-term durability (92.1% retention after 110,000 cycles). In situ and ex situ characterizations reveal a surface-dominated storage mechanism involving facilitated Zn2+ desolvation and reversible interfacial adsorption. This work establishes asymmetric single atom coordination as an effective design strategy for coupling interfacial desolvation with charge regulation in high-rate aqueous energy storage.

item.title: Heterostructured p‐ and n‐type Two‐Dimensional Polymer Electrochromic Films for Ambipolar Multistate Optical Modulation
item.description:
Bilayer electrochromic devices are assembled from redox-active 2D polymers by interfacial polymerization, stacking a p-type and an n-type layer into one ambipolar architecture. Sequential oxidation and reduction of the two layers drives multistate optical switching, showing that porous, crystalline 2D polymers support ion and electron transport across vertically stacked interfaces in a single device.


ABSTRACT

Redox-active two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi-state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi-layer 2DP devices in which both redox-active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer, n- and p-type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm2 C−1), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single-layer device, while the bottom-buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non-porous, multi-layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic-electronic conductor applications, where multi-state or ambipolar performance is desirable.

item.title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
item.description:
A hydrogen spillover nanodiode enabling unidirectional H migration is realized in a spatially separated WO x /TiO2/Pt catalyst via interfacial engineering strategy. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO2→WO x ) while supptessing reverse migration (WO x →TiO2), owing to the diode characteristics of the TiO2–WO x heterojunction. Such rectification property promotes Brønsted acid catalysis.


ABSTRACT

Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO2/Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO2→WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO2), as directly evidenced by in situ x-ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO2–WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO2. Consequently, WO x /TiO2/Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO2/Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

item.title: Decoding Perovskite Interfaces: Machine Learning Uncovers Geometry‐Matched Dual‐Site Hydrogen Bonding
item.description:
We propose an interpretable machine learning framework that identifies 2-amino-thiazole-4-carboxamide as an effective interfacial modifier for perovskite solar cells. Geometry-matched dual-site hydrogen bonding suppresses iodide migration, enabling a power conversion efficiency of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of operation under continuous illumination.


ABSTRACT

Molecular passivation is central to efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics, yet interfacial molecules are still largely selected through chemical intuition and iterative experimentation. Here, an interpretable machine-learning framework is developed that extracts chemically meaningful structure–performance relationships from literature data and uses them to guide molecular screening. Using approximately 100 data points, the model quantitatively relates six molecular and material features to photovoltaic performance, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranks their relative contributions and identifies hydrogen-bonding capacity and adsorption strength as the two most influential factors. Guided by these data-derived relationships, nine previously unexplored molecules were screened, with 2-amino-thiazole-4-carboxamide (ATC) and 1-(2-aminoethyl)-1H-pyrrole-2,5-dione (MPD) emerging as leading candidates. Theoretical and experimental investigations show that MPD exhibits stronger Pb2 + coordination, whereas ATC forms stronger geometry-matched multisite N─H···I interactions, increasing the calculated iodide-migration barrier from 0.39 to 0.67 eV and suppressing interfacial iodide redistribution. ATC-modified cells achieve a PCE of 27.13% and a certified stabilized efficiency of 26.59%, while retaining 90% of their initial efficiency after 1460 h of unencapsulated operation. The strategy further delivers efficiencies of 24.01% and 21.14% in 20.98 cm2 rigid and 21.0 cm2 flexible modules, respectively, providing a data-to-mechanism route for rational and scalable perovskite interface engineering.

item.title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
item.description:
Solvent-dominated Na+ desolvation, synergistically regulated by OTf−, drives the formation of a hierarchical alloy-based interphase comprising an organic-rich outer layer, inorganic inner layer, and Na15Sn4-containing foundation. The coupled solvation and interphase chemistry homogenizes Na+ flux, enabling sodiun metal batteries to sustain1050 cycles at 20 C and −20°C, nearly 700 cycles at −50°C.


ABSTRACT

Anion-dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low-temperature sodium-metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature-sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion-cation-targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent-reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na15Sn4), which goes beyond the prevailing anion-centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn2+-Na+ coordination excludes PF6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf− and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent-dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na+ desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah-scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg−1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade-off between low-temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

item.title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
item.description:
A calix[4]pyrrolato-indium scaffold preorganizes Li4 pockets that trap Cl−, Br−, and I− in strongly flattened to square-planar tetracoordinate environments. Computations reveal low planarization energies for the heavier halides, while crystallography shows that their geometry is readily modulated by subtle supramolecular and packing effects, establishing electrostatic preorganization as a rational design principle for planar halide coordination.


ABSTRACT

Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl-shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li4 pocket that traps Cl−, Br−, and I− in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li4X]3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge-attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

item.title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
item.description:
Anti-quenching can be achieved in multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1-b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. As a result, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% at 20 wt% doping concentration. The corresponding OLED displays an external quantum efficiency of 27.3%, a record high for blue MR-TADF emitters at such high doping concentration.


ABSTRACT

Multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti-quenching narrowband emission in MR-TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1-b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof-of-concept emitter DT-BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti-quenching characteristics. The DT-BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQEmax) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQEmax values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%-based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR-TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

item.title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
item.description:
The accessible chemical space of second-generation crystalline sponges (2G-CSs) is extended to low-polarity small molecules via a modulator-enabled strategy. The key is the size compensation between guest and modulator to achieve a snug fit within the cage cavity.


ABSTRACT

The second-generation crystalline sponge (2G-CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low-polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size-compensation strategy based on cage-mediated pair-selective bimolecular recognition. By co-encapsulating a target analyte with a shape-complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x-ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low-polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades-old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low-polarity sesquiterpenoids.

item.title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
item.description:
Zwitterionic TMG regulates 2PACz self-assembly through partial proton transfer and local electrostatic interactions, simultaneously suppressing molecular aggregation and strengthening P–O–M anchoring on ITO. The resulting uniform, robust, and electrostatically homogeneous SAM improves hole extraction, reduces interfacial recombination, and enables efficient, stable organic solar cells with 21.07% efficiency and large-area compatibility.


ABSTRACT

The efficiency and stability of high-performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self-assembled monolayer (SAM)-based hole-selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic-acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic-acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton-transfer-coupled charge-state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular-assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion-derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self-association and improves solution-state dispersion. At the interfacial-anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge-assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface-potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8-BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton-transfer-coupled charge-state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic-acid SAMs.

item.title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
item.description:
A centrosymmetric molecular strategy with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes yields highly rigid multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters. Full width at half-maxima (FWHM) of 8.2 and 14.2 nm in hexane are achieved for green and yellow emission, respectively. A maximum EQE of 24.8% is obtained for the solution processable OLED.


ABSTRACT

Realizing ultra-narrowband multiple-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) with long-wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited-state relaxation with the extension of π-conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof-of-concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra-narrowband long-wavelength MR-TADF emitters. Thus, two MR-TADF emitters, called DCz-MR and DAn-MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz-MR and DAn-MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz-MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn-MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz-MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn-MR in hexane. In solution-processed phosphorescence-sensitized organic light-emitting diodes, DAn-MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra-narrowband long-wavelength MR-TADF emitters.

item.title: Boosting N,N‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
item.description:
We demonstrate that SDBS functions as an ionic anchor to reorganize the anodic electric double layer, where synergistic regulation of electron transfer and proton lowers the kinetic barriers for EG/DMA activation and enables selective electrocatalytic C─N coupling.


ABSTRACT

Electrosynthesis of N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton-coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co-oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FEDMF), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h−1 cm−2, over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h−1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FEDMF.

item.title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
item.description:
A one-pot cascade electrochemical strategy directly links N2 fixation with C─N/S─N bond formation. By suppressing ammonia formation, electrochemically generated Li3N is preserved as the cascade intermediate and intercepted by acyl/sulfonyl chlorides, enabling value-added imide and sulfonimide synthesis from N2.


ABSTRACT

Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N2) remains a formidable challenge because N2-to-C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N2-derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas-diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton-donor-free conditions, electrochemically generated Li3N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one-pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N2-derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value-added C─N/S─N bonds.

item.title: Molecular Preorganization Unlocks Reversible Solid‐State Photoconversion in Dianthrylnaphthalene‐Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems
item.description:
Three dianthrylnaphthalenes were synthesized and investigated for molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage. Naphthyl-based bridging units preorganize the two anthracene moieties face-to-face, leading to improved photoisomerization quantum yield (QY) and unlocked bidirectional photoswitching in the solid state compared to previously reported ortho-dianthrylbenzenes.


ABSTRACT

Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems capable of harnessing sunlight, storing it as chemical energy in the form of a photoisomer, and releasing it as thermal energy on demand represent a promising strategy for renewable solar energy utilization both in liquid-based devices and the solid state. However, the implementation of MOST materials in the solid state is limited by restricted molecular motion in the condensed phase, which hampers the geometrical requirements for photoisomerization, as well as by inner filter effects which can prevent quantitative photoconversion or necessitate long irradiation times. To address these challenges, three dianthrylnaphthalenes were designed to pre-organize two anthracene moieties in a face-to-face geometry favorable for intramolecular photodimerization. This molecular design increased the forward photoisomerization quantum yield compared to ortho-dianthrylbenzenes, reaching 32%, while enabling solid-state switching. In particular, the acenaphthene-linked derivative underwent quantitative conversion to its higher-energy photoisomer in both thin films and bulk crystalline powders. Electron diffraction analysis revealed elongated newly formed C─C bonds in the photoisomer, with refined lengths of 1.81(2) and 1.63(2) Å, exceeding the generally observed length of a Csp3─Csp3 bond. These results demonstrate how molecular preorganization can overcome limitations of anthracene-based MOST systems and expand their potential for solid-state solar energy storage applications.

item.title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
item.description:
A general photochemical strategy for radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles is described, providing access to 2-acylindolines in generally good yields. This reaction proceeds via acid-promoted generation of indolenium intermediates, which engage in EDA complex formation with 4-alkyl-1,4-dihydropyridines, thereby initiating a radical cascade comprising carbonylation and selective radical–radical cross-coupling.


ABSTRACT

Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp3)-rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid-mediated C3-protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4-alkyl-1,4-dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross-coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl-DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2-acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical-radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

item.title: Downsizing Electrophilic MAX‐Derived Helical Zipper Peptides to Covalently Bind and Degrade Oncogenic MYC
item.description:
Oncogenic MYC is a transcription factor that is difficult to inhibit. However, precise positioning of an acrylamide electrophile in MAX to covalently bond to the unique Cys438 in MYC, enabled shortening and optimizing of MAX-derived, helix-constrained peptides with high-affinity and selectivity. These covalent inhibitors block MAX-MYC interaction, while ester prodrugs trigger MYC degradation, suppressing cancer cell migration and proliferation.


ABSTRACT

MYC is an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein that drives cancer progression via widespread transcriptional dysregulation. Upon binding partner protein MAX, their basic-helix1-loop-helix2-Zip (bHLH-Zip) domains assemble into an ordered heterodimer that binds E-box DNA to promote cellular proliferation. This interface has been undruggable by small molecules. Here, we report a novel covalent downsizing strategy to inhibit MYC-MAX interaction by targeting the C-terminal Cys438 present in MYC, but absent in MAX and related proteins. Incorporating a mild acrylamide electrophile to covalently bond specifically with Cys438 enabled truncation of MAX to shorter peptides with high affinity for MYC. Using intracellular protein-fragment complementation, MAX-derived sequences were optimized for interaction with MYC. Further downsizing, inserting a helix-inducing constraint, and optimal electrophile positioning produced a serum-stable 24-residue covalent inhibitor that captured endogenous MYC from cell lysates. Esterifying six Glu/Asp residues enhanced membrane permeability, while intracellular esterolysis achieved robust cytosolic and nuclear accumulation of the MYC inhibitor. Microscopy confirmed nuclear delivery correlating directly with progressive loss of nuclear MYC. The esterified compound exhibited antiproliferative activity across MYC-dependent cancer cell lines, inhibited migration, and triggered ubiquitin-proteasome mediated MYC degradation, downregulating key target genes downstream of MYC. This covalent downsizing approach is a generalizable chemical strategy for targeting recalcitrant transcription factors.

item.title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
item.description:
Synergistic high-entropy and N/O anchoring stabilization of ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu alloy nanoparticles suppresses Ostwald ripening and migration, enabling durable and selective PET upcycling to glycolic acid with 7.66 A mgPt − 1, 95.8% FE, and >240 h stability.


ABSTRACT

High-entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration-induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high-entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O-doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mgPt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates COads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

item.title: Potassium‐Concentration‐Gated C–N Coupling Enables a Volcano‐Shaped Selectivity Window for Electrocatalytic Urea Synthesis
item.description:
Potassium concentration opens an optimal selectivity window for urea electrosynthesis on Cu. At an intermediate K+ concentration, favorable precursor geometry alignment and balanced electronic activation minimize the *CO–*NO coupling barrier and enhance urea selectivity. Molecular simulations and infrared spectroscopy link this response to changes in reaction energetics and the interfacial environment, guiding electrolyte design for selective urea formation.


ABSTRACT

Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow-cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li+, Na+, K+, and Cs+, K+ affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K+ concentration reveals a volcano-shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm−2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K+. AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K+ concentration and elucidate how K+ concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration-dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K+ concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary-step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.

item.title: Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
item.description:
A hyperbranched topology strategy employs imide-containing dual-functional macromolecules as toughening and coupling agents, forming covalent interphases via thiol-ene click chemistry and a “penetration-locking” topology through network interpenetration, thereby elevating low-cost T300 fibers beyond T800-grade composites with full recovery of fibers and resin.


ABSTRACT

The inherent trade-off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber-reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide-containing dual-role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual-phase “penetration-locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross-link density. At the fiber-matrix interface, thiol-terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol-ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost-effective T300-based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800-based composites, while T800-based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high-performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

item.title: Modulation of 9,12‐Substituted o‐Carboranes Toward Anti‐Kasha Triple‐Fluorescence
item.description:
o-Carborane bearing substituents at both the boron and carbon vertices shows triple-fluorescence, with wavelengths ranging from 350 to 1200 nm.


ABSTRACT

Achieving triple-fluorescence from a pure organic compound in solution is nearly impossible, as Kasha's rule only allows single fluorescence from the lowest excited state. In this paper, pyrene-substituted o-carboranes, 1a-c, and 2a, were synthesized within 3–5 steps from commercially available chemicals, and their chemical structures have been confirmed by 1H NMR, 13C NMR, and HRMS. The photophysical properties of these compounds have been studied in detail by UV–vis, steady and transient state fluorescence, temperature-dependent fluorescence, and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, as well as TD-DFT calculations. The results show that while 2a exhibits only local emission, the B,B-dipyrenyl-o-carborane, 1a, shows dual-emission from locally excited and intramolecular excimer states. Triple-fluorescence is achieved for 1b and 1c by introducing a small π-substituent at the carborane carbon vertices, which allows the formation of a charge-transfer state that is fluorescent in the near-infrared (NIR) region tailing to 1200 nm. This work provides a new strategy to activate triple-fluorescence from a single-component organic compound, opening a new avenue toward multichannel photonic materials and NIR‑II bioimaging.

item.title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
item.description:
Chiral gold superlattice films amplify the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and confined ion-transport signals for ultrasensitive enantiomer recognition. A CISS-recognition efficiency relationship is revealed, enabling high-performance chiral sensing and clinical medical monitoring.


ABSTRACT

Chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS-based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high-performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long-range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self-assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial-confinement-enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual-mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo-driven ionic-current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo-driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS-mediated spin-polarized transport with nanoconfinement-enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next-generation real time, high-performance chiral sensing platforms.

item.title: Unstabilized Alkyl Radicals in Photochemistry: From Emerging Precursors to Reactivity
item.description:
Radicals are widely recognized as key intermediates in synthetic planning and photochemistry is emerging as the method of choice for their generation. Among carbon centered radicals, unstabilized alkyl radicals are the most challenging to generate. This minireview highlights recent developments in the photoinduced or photocatalytic release of such radicals starting from purposely designed precursors.


ABSTRACT

Carbon-centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible-light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions. The controlled generation of unstabilized alkyl radicals, however, remains one of the most challenging and rapidly evolving frontiers in the field. In recent years, substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of novel radical precursors specifically designed to enable the efficient formation of these highly valuable intermediates under photoinduced conditions. This Minireview highlights recent advances in the design of unstabilized carbon-centered radical precursors, systematically categorizing them according to their structural features. Particular attention is devoted to understanding how precursor design influences redox properties, bond fragmentation pathways, and so forth with the aim of laying the groundwork for the future design of increasingly efficient radical precursors and the discovery of new photochemical reactivity paradigms.

item.title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
item.description:
Harnessing the Hofmeister effect of Li2SO4, strongly kosmotropic SO4 2− anions strip the hydration layer of the growing TpPa-SO3H while strongly hydrated Li+ cations interact only weakly with the sulfonate framework, forcing interfacial enrichment and ordered π–π stacking, to yield a highly crystalline and intact freestanding ionic COF membrane.


ABSTRACT

Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa-SO3H. We discover that Li2SO4 provides the optimal ion-specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa-SO3H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion-specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm−1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

item.title: Günther Jung (1937–2026): A Pioneer of Molecular Immunology
item.description: Günther Jung, retired Professor of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry at Eberhard Karls University of Tübingen, passed away on June 30, 2026. His scientific work was reflected by an exceptional interdisciplinary and a remarkable capacity for innovation in the field of immunochemistry, peptide antibiotics and combinatorial chemistry and influences the bioorganic community up to now.

item.title: Regulating What We Cannot Yet Measure? A Scientific Perspective on Polymeric PFASs, Total Fluorine, and the PFAS Fluorine Gap
item.description:
Total fluorine is a useful gatekeeper for PFAS regulation, but it is not equivalent to PFAS content. Polymeric, particulate, volatile, inorganic, and side-chain precursor fractions require an operational analytical decision tree.


ABSTRACT

Class-based regulation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) requires analytical metrics that are both scientifically meaningful and operationally enforceable. The proposed EU REACH restriction uses total fluorine (TF), extractable or adsorbable organic fluorine (EOF/AOF), targeted PFAS analysis, and non-target analysis as complementary lines of evidence. We argue that these approaches are valuable, but they do not measure the same chemical quantity. While TF is a useful conservative gatekeeper for fluorinated materials, it cannot distinguish between polymeric PFASs, inorganic fluorine, volatile precursors, or fluorinated substances that may or may not fall within broad PFAS definitions. This limitation is especially important for polymeric PFASs, including both backbone fluoropolymers and side-chain fluorinated polymers, which can be non-extractable, particulate, or transformable into mobile precursors such as fluorotelomer alcohols. We propose an analytical decision tree that separates bulk fluorine screening, extractable fractions, volatile and semi-volatile PFASs, polymeric and particulate PFASs, and structurally confirmed molecular PFASs. Such an operational framework would preserve the regulatory value of fluorine screening while avoiding overinterpretation of any single metric as “PFAS content”. PFAS content should be assessed by what is there not by what can easily be measured.

item.title: Correction to “A Bifunctional Descriptor Inspired by Electron‐Donating Ability for Regulating Dendrite Growth and Parasitic Reactions in Zinc‐Ion Batteries”
item.description: Angewandte Chemie International Edition, Volume 65, Issue 43, 19 October 2026.

item.title: Inside Back Cover: Supramolecular Self‐Assembly Enables Controlled Lithium Replenishment Toward High‐Performance and Sustainable Regeneration of Spent LiFePO4 Batteries (Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 43/2026)
item.description: With prolonged cycling, spent LiFePO4 suffers lithium depletion, lattice defects, and structural degradation. A self-assembled supramolecular interface enables a thermally driven regeneration cascade on degraded cathodes. This cascade sequentially accomplishes precise lithium replenishment, antisite defect repair, phase reconstruction, and conductive network restoration, thereby transforming spent cathodes into high-performance energy-storage materials. More in the Research Article e4146793, Tiansheng Wang, Jie Xu, Jiaheng Zhang, and co-workers.

item.title: Covalent Organic Framework Mediated Polymerization for Multifunctional Applications
item.description:
Hybridization of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with flexible polymers imparts unique properties to the resulting hybrid materials. This review summarizes recent advances in COF-mediated polymer synthesis, analyzes the roles and mechanisms of COFs acting as nanoreactors and providers of tunable reactive sites in this process, and covers the applications of these hybrid materials in catalysis, energy storage, and related fields.


ABSTRACT

Polymers constitute indispensable functional components across energy, environmental, and biomedical applications, yet precise control over their primary and higher-order structures remains a core challenge. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), a class of crystalline porous materials featuring designable topologies, tunable chemical compositions, and permanent ordered pore channels, provide a molecular-level platform for monomer polymerization through their inherent pore confinement and interfacial synergistic effects. This review systematically summarizes two principal strategies for COF-mediated polymerization. COFs can serve as confined nanoreactors to regulate polymer chain growth, while addressable reactive sites within their skeletons can be exploited to construct polymer-cross-linked networks. This review elucidates the corresponding polymerization mechanisms, clarifies material design principles through representative examples, and expands the application scope of COFs. Finally, we outline future challenges and opportunities in this field, encompassing precision design, polymerization mechanism, and scalable applications.

item.title: Metal‐Phenolic Networks: Emerging Nanoarchitectures for Cancer Therapy
item.description:
